title: Warning Lights, Faults & Breakdowns
whatItIs: Know what every warning display means and never ignore one: it could be a dangerous fault developing. If the car breaks down, protect yourself and warn others.
keyFacts: Warning lights come on with the ignition and go out once the engine starts, except the handbrake light.
A light that stays on, or comes on while driving: stop and investigate. It could be a serious fault.
Charge warning light while driving: the battery may not be charging. Get it checked as soon as possible.
Low brake fluid may result in brake failure and a crash.
Engine overheated? Wait until it has cooled naturally before removing the coolant filler cap.

items.title: Get off the road
items.text: If possible. Stop in a place of relative safety.

items.title: Warn other traffic
items.text: Hazard lights if you're causing an obstruction.

items.title: Warning triangle
items.text: At least 45 m behind, same side of the road.

items.title: Stand clear
items.text: Never between your car and oncoming traffic.

a.label: Tyre bursts while driving
points: Let the car roll to a stop at the side

b.label: Flat tyre
points: Stop as soon as it's safe
Change it only without risk; else call for help

onTheTest.question: Your car catches fire in the engine compartment. What should you do?
options: Get everyone out and call the fire brigade
Open the bonnet to tackle the fire
Drive on to the nearest garage
Pour water into the engine bay
onTheTest.why: Highway Code annex 6: get the occupants out quickly to a safe place. Don't try to put out an engine fire: opening the bonnet will make it flare.

onTheTest.question: Where should a warning triangle go when a car breaks down on an ordinary road?
options: At least 45 metres behind, same side
On the opposite side of the road
At least 45 metres in front of the car
onTheTest.why: Rule 276: put a warning triangle on the road at least 45 metres (147 feet) behind your broken-down vehicle, on the same side of the road.

traps: Never use a warning triangle on a motorway.
Smell of burning rubber, petrol or electrics? Investigate immediately: don't risk a fire.
ABS warning light on? There's a fault with the anti-lock braking system.
